routes.title: Regular round
routes.text: Applying by 1 January means decisions by the end of March.

routes.title: Early round
routes.text: Applying by 1 November means decisions in mid-December and more time for everything after.

usStart.label: When classes begin
usStart.text: Until you enter the start date from your I-20, Pathway assumes 15 August. An early date is the cautious choice, because you may enter the USA only 30 days before it.

usDeadlines.label: Application deadlines
usDeadlines.text: Pathway plans for 1 November (early) and 1 January (regular), Harvard's dates and the first days of the usual ranges. Most universities close between 1 and 15 November, and between 1 and 15 January.

essays.label: Time for essays and applications
essays.text: Pathway plans 20 weeks of essay work for mostly very competitive universities, 12 weeks for a balanced mix, and 8 weeks for mostly less competitive ones. Long lists bring many supplemental essays.

statementBeforeDecision.label: When to print the bank statement
statementBeforeDecision.text: Pathway places the bank statement in the month before decisions, because some universities refuse funding documents older than 6 months.

arriveSpare.label: Arriving before classes
arriveSpare.text: Pathway plans to have you there a week before classes, for orientation.

earlyScores.label: Test scores in the early round
earlyScores.text: Pathway uses Harvard's rule for the early round: test scores may arrive by the end of November. Check each of your universities.

listBefore.label: Choosing your universities
listBefore.text: Pathway suggests settling your list 8 weeks before your first deadline, so every essay is written for a known university. It never uses this to decide that an intake is out of reach.

steps.title: Choose your universities
steps.text: Check each university's own deadline, test policy and aid for international students. Pathway plans for the earliest deadline in each round. When you know your universities' earliest deadline, enter it on "Submit your applications", and this step moves with it.
tasks: Write down each university's exact deadline
Check which ones are need-blind for international students

steps.title: Write your essays
steps.text: The Common App personal essay goes to every university; many also ask for shorter essays of their own.
tasks: Ask two teachers for recommendation letters

steps.title: Complete the CSS Profile
steps.text: Many universities that give aid to international students ask for it when you apply. Fee waivers are generally not open to international students.

steps.title: Submit your applications
steps.text: Your test scores should reach each university by its deadline. Some accept scores a little later; check each one.

steps.title: Your SAT scores reach your universities
steps.text: Harvard accepts early-round scores until the end of November, so a test in early November can still count.

steps.title: Print your bank statement
steps.text: Universities need proof that one year of fees and living costs is covered. Some refuse documents older than 6 months, so this sits just before decisions.

steps.title: Admission decisions arrive
steps.text: Harvard's dates are shown. Check each university's own date.

steps.title: Accept your offer
steps.text: Accepting early starts your I-20 sooner, and every step after it waits for the I-20.
tasks: Pay a deposit if your university asks for one

steps.title: Receive your I-20
steps.text: The wait starts once your university has every document it asks for, so send your funding documents the day you accept.

steps.title: Pay the SEVIS fee and book your visa interview
steps.text: Pay the SEVIS fee the day your I-20 arrives, then book the first interview you can get. Set your social media accounts to public.

steps.title: Print a fresh bank statement
steps.text: Pathway suggests a new statement for the interview, so the officer sees current figures.

steps.title: Your visa interview
steps.text: The wait for an interview in Dhaka changes from month to month. Pathway plans for the longest wait seen in the last 12 months.
tasks: Bring your I-20, passport, statements and admission letter

steps.title: Travel to the USA
steps.text: You may enter the USA up to 30 days before the start date on your I-20, and no earlier.

shaping.tierReach: Your universities are mostly very competitive. So Pathway plans 20 weeks of essays and suggests 12 to 20 applications, including some less competitive universities.
shaping.tierBalanced: Your universities are a balanced mix. So Pathway plans 12 weeks of essays and suggests 8 to 12 applications.
shaping.tierSafe: Your universities are mostly less competitive. So Pathway suggests 5 to 8 applications.
shaping.aidNeed: You need financial aid to go. So the aid steps are in your plan, and a longer list gives you more chances of an affordable offer.
